newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens on excess liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens on excess liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in late trading on Monday, dealers said.
They said trading was slow, with sentiment on the dollar seen improving further on sustained ample rupiah liquidity.
"The underlying tone seems to be biddish for dollars. But operators appear to be taking a cautious stance due to the weekly tax payments on Tuesday," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah edged down to 2,353.40/53.90 at 0930 GMT from an opening of 2,351.5/52.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,353.10/53.65 and 2,351.70/52.00 respectively.
Ample rupiah also caused short-dated swap rates to fall, with overnight swap quoted at 0.20/0.25 and tom/next at 0.27/0.35 points respectively.
Overnight money was last traded at seven percent. The central bank did not offer overnight papers (SBIs) on Monday.
Some dealers said liquidity might remain well supplied on Tuesday on the back of low swap rates.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,349/2,541 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,349/2,397 on Monday as anticipated earlier.
Dealers said it was more profitable to go long on dollars as long as the central bank maintained a three- to four-point rupiah depreciation a week and the swap costs remained cheap.
They said offshore operators seemed to be reducing their short dollar positions due to ample supply and Bank Indonesia's policy of depreciating the rupiah by 3-4 points a week.
One-month swaps was at 15.25/15.75, two at 28.75/30.00, three at 42.0/42.5 and six at 85.75/86.25 points.
